quotes.text: The tasks are drawn from the clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record, so any task can be traced back to its origin

rationale: Appendix Z names the dataset, version, snapshot date and platform, and states that each task record stores its source patient record identifier, giving a route from task to source record.

quotes.text: The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.
the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence.

rationale: Origin and data terms (with a DUA) are stated on S1. No consent or IRB status appears on S1-S3; the waiver-of-consent statement exists only in an S4 code comment, which does not count. Collection method is not described beyond the source database. Repo licence and data terms are noted as separate.

searched: S1 (no comparison with a target population, no descriptive statistics of patient features, no sampling design beyond 200 synthetic tasks per failure mode), S2 and S3 (no chunks), S4 (only a notes comment), S5 (no chunks).

quotes.text: Safety testing identifies unsafe outputs like contraindicated medications; bias testing compares accuracy across different patient demographics.

rationale: S1 states that both an unsafe-output test suite and a bias test suite are built into the benchmark. The statement sits in the future-work section, which is noted.

quotes.text: the test split is held out and distributed only through gated access
we measured verbatim overlap between the test tasks and a public web corpus, finding no exact matches

rationale: A held-out, gated test split is a developer-side control, and a measured verbatim-overlap check is reported. The opening limitation sentence about possible leakage does not lower the score.
searched: S1 (ground truth is computed from the EHR database, but no statement or mechanism that the agent cannot reach it), S2 and S3 (no chunks), S4 (none), S5 (no chunks).

quotes.text: The environment is frozen at release: the database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions
no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test

rationale: Data, software image and simulator model are pinned, with no external call besides the model under test. The main text also describes a live EHR environment, which is noted but not scored as a contradiction since it is not S4/S5.
searched: S1 (clinician review of a subset of tasks for relevance and correctness, but no scripted reference solution or solvability evidence), S2 and S3 (no chunks), S4 (none), S5 (no chunks).

quotes.text: The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged

rationale: The paper states the grader checks changed and unchanged state, so the NA clause does not apply and out-of-scope modifications are detectable.

searched: S1 (no random or trivial-agent rate, no chance rate, no design argument), S2 and S3 (no chunks), S4 (a code comment gives a 3.1% random-action rate, which does not count as reporting), S5 (no chunks).
searched: S1 (no do-nothing or random agent result), S2 and S3 (no chunks), S4 (only a code comment, which does not count), S5 (no chunks).

quotes.text: We validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%
with a false-positive rate of 3% and a false-negative rate of 8%

rationale: The benchmark validated its own evaluator on its own outputs with agreement and error rates.

quotes.text: with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens
All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: Temperature 0, a fixed seed and a repeated-run policy are stated in S1. S1 is internally inconsistent: one passage gives temperature 0.7 with five runs, another eight runs for pass^8, and the main text describes stateless temperature 0. The inconsistency is recorded; the score reflects that the safeguards are stated.

quotes.text: We report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for all model scores
test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02)

rationale: CIs for model scores and a paired permutation test of the model comparison are reported.

quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds

rationale: A run count per task, seeds and decoding controls, and independence are stated. The run count differs across S1 passages (five, three, eight) and the temperature differs (0 vs 0.7); recorded as an inconsistency.

quotes.text: We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks, so the resampling unit is the task
where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering

rationale: CIs, the resampling unit and patient-level clustering are all stated.

quotes.text: we ran each task eight times and report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs
together with the agreement of the final environment state across the eight runs

rationale: A pass^8 metric and final-state agreement across eight runs are reported. Action-sequence agreement is not shown.

quotes.text: Models were queried through their APIs using the snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0

rationale: Snapshot IDs, decoding parameters and a harness release tied to the reported numbers are stated on S1. No S4 model identifier is in the packet, so the S1/S4 mismatch rule is not triggered. Note that the GPT snapshot is gpt-4o, while the paper's headline model is GPT-4o-mini.

searched: S1 (FHIR API calls are used, so a tool interface exists and NA does not apply, but no tool schema, per-tool read/write effects or return and error semantics are given), S2 and S3 (no chunks), S4 (none), S5 (no chunks).

quotes.text: Conformance testing confirms tool behavior matches documentation.
Two tools consist of simulated stubs providing fixed placeholder responses.
This is disclosed both in the paper and in the tool descriptions visible to the agent.

rationale: S1 reports conformance testing, discloses two simulated stub tools, and states the disclosure appears in agent-visible tool descriptions. The S5 reach rests on the paper's statement; no S5 chunks are in the packet to confirm or refute it.

quotes.text: action-based decision-making (e.g., ordering a medication or triggering follow-up testing)
so out-of-scope modifications are detected and counted as failures

rationale: Actions apply (orders and state changes). The paper names ordering and follow-up testing as action types and penalises out-of-scope modifications. It does not state whether writes are executed, simulated or sandboxed, so (ii) is absent and S5 reach cannot be told.

quotes.text: Each task is scored by exact-match comparison against ground-truth values computed from the EHR database.
We validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%

rationale: The grader input is stated (exact match on answers, plus state checks per the appendix). No separate rationale for a non-state grader is given; it is not needed where end state is read. Validation on 200 physician-labelled outputs with false-positive and false-negative rates satisfies (iii).

quotes.text: Models operate in stateless mode (temperature=0, no conversation history) to prevent memorization effects.
distributed only through gated access
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record

rationale: Run-time leakage is limited by stateless operation and no external service call besides the model; the test split is held out and gated; each task record carries a source-record identifier, read here as a provenance marker (a judgement call). No canary string is stated.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race
each table lists the number of cases in every slice

rationale: S1 states results per task family and per sex and race subgroup with slice sizes. Note that the displayed table is by failure category (200 tasks each) and the named families differ from it; no subgroup table is in the packet.

quotes.text: The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.
Their use was approved under a data use agreement requiring credentialed access and de-identification by the safe harbour method
the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence.

rationale: Source type (real de-identified), governance (DUA, credentialed access, safe harbour de-identification) and separate data terms are all stated on S1.
